metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent searched 'Diamond' on recreation.gov homepage, selected the first autocomplete result, and navigated to the Diamond campground page. Screenshot 13 tab title shows 'Diamond, Uinta-Wastch...' confirming the tab title contains 'Diamond'.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can type into recreation.gov search bar, select autocomplete suggestions, navigate to campground page. Tab title confirmed to contain 'Diamond' from step 4 trajectory reasoning and screenshot 13.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at step 13+ due to horizontal calendar scroll confusion. The campground page navigation itself was reliably completed by step 4.
metadata.task_rationale: Uses page title as an additional signal beyond URL. Screenshot 13 shows Chrome tab titled 'Diamond, Uinta-Wastch...' confirming 'Diamond' appears in the browser tab title when the correct campground page is open. This is a stronger check than URL alone.
metadata.explanation: Custom metric check_recreation_title checks: (1) URL contains 'recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/', AND (2) browser tab title contains 'Diamond'. Returns 1.0 if both, 0.5 if URL only. Tab title 'Diamond' is confirmed from screenshot 13. Initial state (recreation.gov homepage, title 'Recreation.gov - Campi...') will fail title check.

scoring_breakdown.url_and_title: 1.0 - On campground URL AND title includes Diamond
scoring_breakdown.url_only: 0.5 - On campground URL but title does not include Diamond

llm_judge_reasons: The URL fragment check ('recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/') correctly verifies the user navigated to a campground page on recreation.gov.
The title keyword check ('Diamond') verifies the opened page is the Diamond campground specifically.
The initial state (recreation.gov homepage) fails both checks, providing proper negative control resistance.
The active_tab_info getter correctly retrieves the live URL and title from the browser, enabling runtime verification.
The metric logic is straightforward: 1.0 for both URL+title match, 0.5 for URL-only, 0.0 for neither.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The 0.5 partial credit for URL-only match could reward landing on any campground page (not necessarily Diamond); consider raising the URL-only threshold or dropping partial credit to make scoring stricter.
The active_tab_info getter re-navigates to the URL, which could theoretically redirect on dynamic sites; acceptable here since recreation.gov campground pages are stable.
